results.notes: WS25-S9 gateway enforcement and the capability-core extension allow-list are built behind ORG_AGENT_POLICY_MODE (default off; shadow observes; any other value enforces) and ORG_EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST (default off; literal true only). Gateway: the org document is read through capability-core GET /api/v1/org-agent-policy with a 30 s TTL and D8 stale bounds (900 s restrictive, 120 s permissive). A Do run whose policy cannot be read is refused with org_policy_unavailable; a plain turn keeps its floor. The org mode cap binds a turn whether or not the person chose a mode, and a choice cannot loosen it; lockdown refuses Do runs with mode_lockdown. Fresh-run rungs are held to the rung cap (an explicit cap when there is no grant), and recorded grants are clamped. Runs are attributed to the held policy revision. Capability-core: the signed gate denies MCP tools whose server is outside ext.mcp_servers (org_extension_not_allowed), approved_only tool approval requires a pinned definition, and the MCP server listing hides disallowed servers, which also feeds the gateway MCP catalogue. With the switches off the paths are unchanged: no network call, resolve_turn returns None when no mode is chosen and the cap is default, clamp and stamp pass through, and the Go rule is never read. Status is done for the code and unit tests. Two capability-core wiring shared edits (lead_todo 1-2) and the live proof (lead_todo 7) are lead-run; until item 1 lands the Go allow-list is not reachable. No docker, no DB harness, no commit, no push.
